Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 25-Nov-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  THIRD SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  OBJECT ORIENTED PROGRAMMING [CSE_2124]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Analyze how primitive and non-primitive (reference) data types differ in Java with respect to          (5)  
  memory allocation, assignment behavior, and comparison operations. Use examples to illustrate  
  A)           how these differences can affect program logic, performance, and debugging.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Write a Java program that demonstrates the use of all eight primitive data types. Initialize each type (5)  
  with a sample value, and show at least one example of type casting between compatible types.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Analyse the structural and behavioral differences between interfaces and abstract classes in Java.     (5)  
  Compare their use cases and evaluate how enhancements in Java 8 and later-such as default and  
  A)           static methods-impact interface design. Use examples to illustrate how these features influence  
  code architecture and flexibility  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Write a Java program that defines an interface Payment with a method processPayment(double             (5)  
  amount). Create two classes, CreditCard and UPI, that implement Payment and provide their own  
  logic for processing payments. In the main method, create objects of both classes and call  
  processPayment() with sample amounts.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)                Write a short Java program where two threads attempt to update a shared counter without                (5)  
  synchronization, and then modify it to use a synchronized method to ensure thread safety.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Discuss the following for writing exception handling code in Java.                                     (5)  
  
  Catching specific exceptions vs generic ones  
  Avoiding empty catch blocks  
  Using finally for resource cleanup  
  Logging exceptions effectively  
  When to use custom exceptions  
  
  Support your answer with suitable examples.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  Page #1

4)                        Write a generic method printArray() that takes an array of any type and prints its elements.            (5)  
  Demonstrate the method with arrays of Integer, String, and Double.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)                Analyse the structure and component interaction in a JavaFX program that extends the Application        (5)  
  class. Break down how Label, StackPane, and Scene work together to render a window titled 'My  
  First JavaFX App' with the message 'Welcome to JavaFX!'. Use a code snippet to illustrate how  
  these elements contribute to the overall GUI layout and lifecycle.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)                        CERT recommends avoiding expressions with side effects in conditional statements. Explain why           (5)  
  using assignments or method calls that modify state inside if, while, or for conditions can lead to  
  A)                unpredictable behavior.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)                Apply the concept of encapsulation by designing a Java class that protects its data using access        (5)  
  modifiers and getter/setter methods. Use a real-world analogy to guide your design and  
  demonstrate how encapsulation supports modularity and data protection through a relevant  
  example.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  -----End-----
